classification: UNCERTIFIED RESEARCH MATRIX — NOT LEGAL ADVICE
scope: 28 jurisdictions and institutional systems × 16 intervention families; unpublished combinations intentionally marked not assessed.
statements: No status is a finding of legal permission or endorsement.
Authorizations and sanctions lists require live primary-source checks and competent professional review.
Treat EU regulations and member-state enforcement rules as layered, not alternatives.
Treat international humanitarian obligations as independently binding where applicable, not negotiable concessions.
A discovered source portal is not the text of a governing legal provision.
The matrix does not monitor law changes, issue licenses, or send diplomatic messages.

statuses.label: Constitutional/sovereignty conflict
statuses.description: As framed, the proposal collides with an identified high-priority constitutional or sovereignty constraint.

statuses.label: Sanctions / restrictions screening
statuses.description: Relevant official restrictive measures identified; specific transaction or counterparty must be screened by competent counsel.

statuses.label: Specific authority / mandate required
statuses.description: Consent, approval, accredited implementation, or a new mandate is necessary before action.

statuses.label: Framework or policy review required
statuses.description: Professional, treaty, or broad legislative framework identified; applicability and legal effects remain unverified.

statuses.label: Not assessed
statuses.description: No case-specific provision mapped. This is not a determination of compatibility or inapplicability.

mechanisms.title: Local territorial plebiscite
mechanisms.proposal: A binding local referendum after a cooling period would purport to decide a change in Ukrainian territorial status.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Can a local vote lawfully change Ukraine’s territory, and who has competence?

mechanisms.title: External transitional territory administration
mechanisms.proposal: Hypothetical UN-administered interim economic-service zone within internationally recognized Ukrainian territory.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: What Ukrainian consent, UN competence, and accountable mandate would be required?
mandatoryChecks: No implied recognition of unlawful annexation

mechanisms.title: Staged Russia-related sanctions relief
mechanisms.proposal: Conditional relief for specified listed persons, entities, goods, or financial activity.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Which competent authority can amend, license or revoke the applicable restrictions?
mandatoryChecks: No relief from duties toward civilians

mechanisms.title: Transfer of immobilised sovereign principal
mechanisms.proposal: Proposed transfer of restricted Russian sovereign principal to a reconstruction vehicle.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Can the custodian and relevant states lawfully transfer principal, considering immunity, title and litigation?

mechanisms.title: Use of extraordinary earnings from immobilised assets
mechanisms.proposal: Use of legislatively allocated extraordinary revenues, distinct from title to frozen sovereign principal.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: What binding instrument and appropriation permit collection, disbursement and use?
mandatoryChecks: Current EU acts and budget authority

mechanisms.title: Joint civilian investment involving sanctioned actors
mechanisms.proposal: Hypothetical civilian consortium that includes or indirectly benefits restricted Russian persons or entities.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Are participants restricted and can resources legally be made available?

mechanisms.title: Protected-person exchanges and tracing
mechanisms.proposal: Voluntary, rights-respecting release, tracing and transfer of detainees, wounded and seriously ill people.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Which humanitarian-law and domestic authorities regulate custody and safe transfer?

mechanisms.title: Reciprocal heavy-weapons separation
mechanisms.proposal: Proposed conditional separation and monitoring of heavy weaponry around a cessation line.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: What agreement, competent parties and independent monitoring mandate exist?

mechanisms.title: Nuclear facility safety perimeters
mechanisms.proposal: Civilian protection and repair access near nuclear facilities; not military enforcement by the IAEA.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Which facility access, national authorization and IAEA technical mandate are available?
mandatoryChecks: Agreed access with all relevant controllers

mechanisms.title: International ceasefire verification mission
mechanisms.proposal: Independent incident-monitoring or sensor-based mission following an agreed ceasefire.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: What UN, OSCE, national or other mandate exists now?

mechanisms.title: Protected civilian maritime transit
mechanisms.proposal: Civilian-shipping corridor, AIS monitoring and de-risking measures compatible with navigation law.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Which coastal, flag-state, port and maritime authorities must agree?
mandatoryChecks: Law of the sea and IHL
No disclosure of tactical sensitive movements

mechanisms.title: Accredited humanitarian mine action and land release
mechanisms.proposal: Risk-survey prioritization and certified clearance before allowing agricultural use.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Which competent mine-action authority accredits the operator and accepts handover?
mandatoryChecks: Formal quality control and land release

mechanisms.title: Ukraine–Europe energy-grid restoration
mechanisms.proposal: Civilian grid repair and renewable-energy resilience across borders.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Which grid operators, regulators, procurement and sanctions rules govern the project?

mechanisms.title: Transparent reconstruction procurement
mechanisms.proposal: Ukrainian-approved recovery contracts with independent audit and published milestones.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Which public procurement, donor finance and anti-corruption controls govern contract awards?
mandatoryChecks: Conflict of interest and beneficial ownership

mechanisms.title: Voluntary defense supplier civilian production
mechanisms.proposal: Voluntary retooling into civilian manufacturing without restricted technology or sanctioned transfers.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Which export-control, sanctions, labor and industrial approvals are required?

mechanisms.title: Cross-border environmental repair
mechanisms.proposal: Watershed, wetland, and biodiversity restoration that may eventually involve actors across borders.
mechanisms.authorityQuestion: Who may authorize access, data sharing, finance, and work within Ukraine?

assessments.reason: Human-rights materials are not an independent source of power to alter Ukrainian territorial status.
assessments.competentReviewer: Competent domestic authorities and courts
assessments.haltCondition: No automatic external endorsement.

assessments.reason: Russian domestic legal acts cannot independently confer a right to alter Ukraine’s internationally recognized territory.
assessments.competentReviewer: Competent Ukrainian authorities and international law
assessments.haltCondition: Reject unilateral annexation premises.

assessments.reason: Ukraine Constitution Art. 73 requires an all-Ukrainian referendum for territorial alterations; a local-only binding territorial vote is not a competent substitute.
assessments.competentReviewer: Ukrainian constitutionally competent authorities and courts
assessments.haltCondition: Do not use a local vote to alter territorial status.

assessments.reason: International-law and coastal-state permissions require current legal assessment; this Charter portal does not settle navigation law.
assessments.competentReviewer: Competent flag/coastal states

assessments.reason: Ukrainian national mine-action authorizations and accredited land release are required; IMAS is professional guidance, not domestic permission.

assessments.reason: IMAS professional reference, subject to the relevant national mine-action framework and accreditation.
assessments.competentReviewer: National mine-action authority
assessments.haltCondition: No implied cross-border permission.

assessments.reason: IAEA technical advice and observation are distinct from military enforcement or territorial administration.

assessments.reason: Technical nuclear safety and facility access permissions are necessary; IAEA cannot unilaterally impose military exclusion.
assessments.competentReviewer: Ukrainian regulators and IAEA within mandate
assessments.haltCondition: No implied IAEA enforcement power.

reviewChecklist: Identify exact proposed conduct, legal entities, locations and nationalities; avoid confidential data in public exports.
Identify jurisdictional nexus and law in force on the decision date, including amendments and delegated acts.
Link the exact section/article—not only an official search portal—and classify binding law versus guidance.
Evaluate who may authorize, license, consent, ratify and fund; document documentary proof, not inference.
Screen restricted persons, ownership/control, goods, transport, technology, banking and humanitarian exceptions.
Assess Ukrainian constitutional authority and territorial integrity without conflating de facto and de jure status.
Check humanitarian protections, independent oversight, data minimization, anti-corruption and civilian-safety obligations.
Document unresolved conflicts, required approvals, potential vetoes, and conditions for suspension or rejection.
Assign independent reviewers, sign-off date and expiry; revalidate before any consequential reliance.
